newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly up on Wednesday with two new companies on the domestic A share market sucking money out of the repo market, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active three-day contract rocketed to 24.91 percent from 14.36 percent on Tuesday.
Turnover rose sharply to 10.92 million lots from 7.25 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
"Volume surged today, indicating institutions borrowed much more funds to speculate on the A share market, which has become more active recently," one trader said.

One new A share firm, Anhui Heli Co was listed on the Shanghai bourse today and the other, Liaoning Jingdi Construction Group Co issued shares, becoming the major reason for institutional borrowing, traders said.
"The rates have become very high after today's surges and they are likely to fall tomorrow on a technical correction," a second trader said.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly down due to profit-taking after a short-lived technical rebound in the past few trading days, traders said.
But the most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 closed unchanged at 121.86 yuan.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market shrank to 1.22 million lots from 2.64 million.
Traders said market sentiment was poor with most investors expecting falling inflation in China to push down coupons for future T-bill and T-bond issues in the short term.
"The market is dominated by short-lined speculators," an analyst said. "The contracts are likely to consolidate down in the short term on expected institutional selling."
